paper.title: Online Matrix Completion: A Collaborative Approach with Hott Items

settings.name_in_paper: Setting 1 (General Regret): online low-rank matrix completion, S=1
unmapped: M users and N items; at each round every user is recommended one item and the reward is observed
unknown rank-r expected reward matrix R in [-1,1]^{M x N}
hott items (separability) assumption: all item embeddings lie in convex hull of r hott item embeddings and 0
offline matrix completion oracle assumption (incoherence / condition number / subset strong smoothness)
r, sigma, kappa (min cluster size fraction) treated as constants
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in [\s{T}]$, for each user $u\in [\s{M}]$, $\s{S}$ carefully chosen distinct items ... are recommended and we observe $\s{S}$ rewards ... $\fl{P}^{(t)}_{u\rho_u(t,j)} = \fl{R}_{u\rho_u(t,j)}+\fl{E}^{(t)}_{u\rho_u(t,j)}$ ... i.i.d zero-mean sub-Gaussian ... Setting 1: We consider $\s{S}=1$

settings.name_in_paper: Setting 2 (Simplified Regret): S=r items recommended per user, non-negative embeddings
unmapped: M users and N items; each round every user is recommended r distinct items and all r rewards observed
regret per round is best item reward minus max reward over the r recommended items, averaged over users
rank-r reward matrix R = U V^T with rows of U and V in the simplex (non-negative embeddings)
learner knows number of users M and items N
settings.definition_quote: Setting 2 (Simplified Regret): Next, we consider a related setting with $\s{S}=r$ ... $\s{Reg}_{\s{Simple}} \triangleq \frac{1}{\s{M}} \Big(\sum_{u}\s{T}\mathbf{R}_{u\pi_u(1)}- \sum_{t,u}\max_{j\in [\s{r}]}\mathbf{R}_{u\rho_u(t,j)}\Big)$

symbols.Delta_hott: hott item gap minimized over most opinionated users of each cluster
symbols.Delta_min: paper's Delta: min over users of gap between best and second-best item

conditions: offline matrix completion oracle assumption A3 (incoherence, condition number, subset strong smoothness)
rank-r reward matrix with entries in [-1,1]

source.label: thm:first
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions \ref{assum:hott}, \ref{assum:simplicity}, \ref{assum:matrix2} are true. Then Alg.\ref{alg:full} (\textsc{PhasedClusterElim}) guarantees the regret $\s{Reg}$ (eq. \eqref{eq:general}) to be $\widetilde{O}\Big(\max\Big(1,\s{N}\s{M}^{-1}\Big)\Big(\Delta_{\s{hott}}^{-2}+\Delta^{-1}\Big)+1\Big)$.

results.notes: Regret is per-user average, defined via expected rewards (pseudo-regret); proof gives the bound with probability 1-delta, statement doesn't specify. Each user's comparator is its own best item. Polylog T and poly(r,sigma,kappa) hidden.

symbols.r_rank: rank of the reward matrix (= number of items recommended per round)
symbols.Delta_det: determinant gap det^2(V_A) - max_{A' != A} det^2(V_A')
symbols.c_avg: average of det^2(U_I) over all r-subsets I of users

conditions: user and item embeddings non-negative with rows in the simplex (Assumption 4)

source.label: thm:second
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions \ref{assum:hott}, \ref{assum:non-negative} are true. Then Alg.\ref{algo:simple} (\textsc{DeterminantElim}) guarantees regret $\s{Reg}_{\s{Simple}}$ (eq. \eqref{eq:simple}) to be $\widetilde{O}\Big(\frac{\sigma^2\s{N}}{c_{\s{avg}}c_{\s{max}}\s{M}^{1/r}\Delta_{\s{det}}}+1\Big)$

results.notes: Proof gives explicit O(1 + sigma^2 N log(MT) 2^{r+1} r^{(r+7)/2}/(M^{1/r} c_avg c_max Delta_det)). Regret per user, max over r recommended items. For r=1 recovers Jain & Pal.

cited_results.setting_description: Online low-rank matrix completion, M users, N items, one item per user per round
Online matrix completion with rank-1 reward matrix
